pets.title: Caught going soft, after four years of saying no dog
pets.note: Caught, as if found out. The photograph and the lean in the yard settle it before the argument ends, and the goodnight ritual is the tenderness she would once have laughed at. Home now has the dog in its description.
pets.description: The one who said no dog finds herself talking to one at half six, won over before she would admit it

pets.title: Goodnight out loud, and two thumps back
pets.description: A ritual too ridiculous to skip

pets.title: The first year's regret, never said
pets.note: It went away, mostly. It comes back on wet Sunday nights, and her partner has never heard it.
pets.description: Thinking it a mistake, and never able to say so about a dog with a past

pets.title: Out on the lane, where the day becomes hers
pets.note: The walk she resented the first year is now the part of the day that is hers. She watches the dog's nose and the bad mood does not survive it.
pets.description: Forty minutes nobody can claim, her head quiet beside a dog's joy in a wet hedge

pets.title: Letting her run, and ageing at the gate
pets.description: Her freedom weighed against the worry every morning, and always let go

pets.title: Closest on the night it cost her something
pets.note: The bad night proves what the easy days cannot. The rules of the house are kept without a word between them.
pets.description: Turning back together in the rain, an agreement neither of them wrote down

pets.title: Five years of it never getting said
pets.note: The morning row is never had because the wag takes it away, and the half nine list is closed with a chin on a knee. She holds both readings open: good for them, or a way round each other.
pets.description: A dog who takes the mood off her, and a couple who talk about the dog instead

pets.title: Cracking first at twenty past six
pets.description: Who gets up, and what being the one who always goes says

pets.title: A dog between them at half nine
pets.note: Two ways at once, her own words for it, and the answer changes with the week.
pets.description: The voices, the list nobody starts, and not knowing which it is

pets.title: Wanted at the door, and finding the dog is easier
pets.note: Being wanted, plainly, is what brings her home. Her partner's remark lands, and she will not pretend it is not true: the dog needs nothing to have been got right.
pets.description: A welcome like no other brings her home, and says something about the people there

pets.title: Coming home for the dog, and what that says
pets.description: Easier than a person, and kinder to her than to the people in the house

pets.title: Grieving in advance a dog who is snoring at her
pets.note: The drive to the vet shows her the size of it, and the thorn makes it a rehearsal. She stops the thought every time, and laughs at herself for grieving a sleeping dog.
pets.description: A thorn shows her the end already rehearsed, and a house that goes flat without her

pets.title: A house on standby without her
pets.note: The quiet is wrong. Two hours flat, and the thought of longer is the one she does not finish.
pets.description: Two hours at the groomer's and the home is a set, furniture waiting

groups.label: Days run to the dog's clock, given a shape or closed in
groups.note: Each day starts when the dog says. Mabel is given a start and a shape, Juno a part of the day that is hers, and Rowan a timetable that closes round him. Convergence in the hour, divergence in what it gives. For Rowan the same early start is fear kept at bay, and the hours have not left him.
groups.description: A start and a shape for Mabel and Juno, a closing timetable for Rowan

groups.label: A reason nobody argues with, letting people in or keeping them out
groups.note: The dog stands between each of them and other people. It opens the estate to Mabel, and for Rowan and Juno it becomes the good reason that keeps others at a distance. The same phrase in two cases, a reason nobody argues with. Mabel's divergence matters: for her the dog is the way back in.
groups.description: Mabel's way back to people, and Rowan's and Juno's way of keeping them off

groups.label: A house lit up by a dog, and flat without one
groups.note: The dog makes the house a home with someone in it. Mabel has the lights on again and someone to tell, Juno is wanted at the door and finds the house on standby without her, and Rowan keeps a bowl under the sink. Presence felt rather than seen, in all three. For Juno and Rowan the empty house is part of the theme: two hours of it for her, every day since June for him.
groups.description: Lights on and a welcome at the door, and a house gone flat without

groups.label: Losing each other, rehearsed, lived through and written into a will
groups.note: Each of them meets the end of the bond in a different tense. Juno rehearses a death still to come, Rowan has given his dog up and cannot settle it, and Mabel expects to go first and has put her dog's future in writing. Three tenses of one loss. Rowan's watchfulness outlasting the dog sits here, the loss lived in the body.
groups.description: A death rehearsed, a dog given up, a future written into a will

groups.label: Holding on to the dog when keeping her costs something
groups.note: Keeping the dog has a price for each of them. Mabel keeps Pepper against her daughter after a broken wrist, Juno pays in worry and in a regret she has never said, and for Rowan the price grows too high and he gives her up. The divergence is the finding here: two of them hold on and one lets go, and none of them blames the dog.
groups.description: Two hold on at a price, and one lets go and cannot settle it
